belief: God took my loved one because He needed them more than I did.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that God took your loved one because He needed them more than you did, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Comforting sayings at funerals: “God needed another angel” or “God needed them more.” Searching for a reason behind a painful loss. Feeling that God chose against you. Anger or confusion about why someone was taken so soon. Trying to make sense of a death that seems senseless.
teaches: This saying is often meant kindly, but Scripture does not teach it. God does not need anything; He gives life and breath to everyone. Death is called “the last enemy,” not a sign of God’s greed. Jesus wept at His friend’s grave. God holds our times in His hands, and we may not understand why a loved one died, but we can know that God did not take them because He needed them more than you. He grieves with you and will one day destroy death forever.
self_statements: God needed them more than I did.
God chose to take them from me.
God must not care about my pain.
I wasn’t important enough to keep them.
God wanted them in heaven, so He took them.
I’m angry at God for taking them.
errors: Assuming you know why God allowed the death.
Picturing God as needy or selfish.
Feeling that God chose against you personally.
Treating a funeral phrase as Scripture.
questions: Does God need anything, according to Acts 17:25?
How did Jesus respond to death at Lazarus’ grave?
Is this saying from the Bible or from well-meaning people?
Can I bring my anger and confusion honestly to God?
Do I need to know why, or can I trust God without knowing?
What does God promise to do with death in the end?
truth: God did not take my loved one because He needed them more than I did. God needs nothing. Death is an enemy that Jesus will destroy. I may not understand why my loved one died, but I know God grieves with me, heals the brokenhearted, and will one day wipe away every tear.
hw_questions: How did Jesus respond to death?
Is this saying from Scripture or people?
Can I bring my anger to God?
Can I trust God without knowing why?
hw_truths: God does not need anything; He gives life.
Death is an enemy that Jesus will destroy.
Jesus weeps with those who grieve.
I can trust God without knowing why.
God will wipe away every tear.
log: Each day, write one honest feeling about my loss and one truth about God.
name_example: He heals Sarah’s broken heart and binds up her wounds.

tracker: One honest prayer about my loss
prayer: Father, I miss my loved one so much. Help me reject the idea that You took them because You needed them more than I did. Thank You that You need nothing, that You grieve with me, and that You will destroy death forever. Heal my broken heart. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
